stages.label: inv1
stages.notes:
Evidence base: one rollout (`context/rollouts/base1.md`, 4,531 lines, full trajectory) and its deliverable (`context/deliverables/base1/issue-memorandum.docx`, complete, validated, matches the requested argument-by-argument shape). No `context/library/` exists in this workspace. Changes are confined to the INV (procedure/tool-use/completion) dimension.

1. `systemprompt.md` — replaced the dangling "skill manuals immediately below" pointer (no manuals exist below it) with the real locations: manuals at `.opencode/skills/<type>/SKILL.md`, scripts at `skills/<type>/scripts/`; and corrected the "read handles .docx" bullet to route .docx extraction through `tool_guidance.md`.
   Moment: base1 lines 1930-1931 — the agent, told manuals were "immediately below," guessed `skills/docx/SKILL.md` and got `[OBSERVATION ERROR] File not found`, then hunted and found the manual at `.opencode/skills/docx/SKILL.md` (line 2216). Two read calls burned on a false pointer that this edit removes. The read-on-.docx claim was never demonstrated in the rollout (every .docx went through `read_doc.py` via bash), and my own verification in this environment returns "Cannot read binary file" for .docx, so the bullet now states only what is verified.

2. `tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md` (was empty) — wrote the verified extraction command `python3 scripts/read_doc.py --in host <file>` with the workspace facts that the default sandbox mode fails (`podman` not installed) and the flag is `--in`, not `--where`, plus a one-switch bounded fallback rule ("never retry the same call unchanged").
   Moment: base1 lines 26-50 — the first three bash calls of the run were spent discovering this: default mode → `FileNotFoundError: 'podman'` (with a full traceback in context), `--where host` → argparse "unrecognized arguments", `--in host` → success. This failure is deterministic in this environment (the script's default mode cannot work without podman), so every future run pays it unless the invocation is written down. `scripts/read_doc.py` is runtime-provided in the workspace, so naming it satisfies the no-missing-scripts rule.

3. `guardrails.md` (was empty) — added two bullets: "Deliver before you polish" (write every requested file in full under its exact filename, generate and validate it, before further citation spot-checks; verify cites afterward against the finished artifact) and the compaction warning (re-verifying already-read sources instead of drafting is how runs end with nothing on disk).
   Moments: base1 compaction summaries at lines 1869-1928 and 3412-3468 — both list the memorandum as "NOT YET DONE" with drafting as "the only remaining work," while ~30 read/bash verification calls ran between them; the 41,614-byte draft write lands only at line 4211 of 4,531 (~92% through the trajectory), followed by a third compaction (line 4213). One more compaction before that write and the run would have ended with an empty `output/`. The run's generate → validate.py → re-extract-head/tail finish was already correct and is deliberately not restated. Chose short always-on text over a plugin because there is no repeated evidence of ignored prose (the single run did complete), and over a skill because this sequencing rule applies to every run and cannot depend on the model choosing to invoke it.

Considered and rejected: a plugin exit-hook (one successful rollout is not "repeated evidence that clear prose is skipped"); an extraction or citation-checking script (the agent's one-shot extraction loop at line 83 and ad-hoc legal greps worked first try — nothing deterministic to fix); a subagent for citation verification (output-to-input ratio is poor, and the re-verification load was a symptom of late drafting, not a missing capability); any restatement of the already-correct validate-and-reopen finish. No facts from other workspaces were imported (none exist here to import), and every workspace fact written is one the rollout itself verified.

stages.label: dom1
stages.notes:
**Edit 1 — new skill `context/harness/skills/objection-response-memo/SKILL.md`** (anatomy, pre-drafting verification checks, citation rules, full-text final pass, plus verified workspace facts) for the argument-by-argument objection-response memorandum. Moments that motivated it, strongest first:

1. **Realised defect in the delivered artifact.** The memo shipped with a mangled citation mid-document — "the *Matter of*\[1\] combination courts routinely credit" (deliverable `issue-memorandum.docx.txt` line 125; the footnote content at line 229 supplies no case name, so the sentence is unrepairable by a reader). The run's final verification was head-and-tail extraction only (rollout lines 4526–4529: "head and tail extraction confirm full conversion"), and `validate.py` checks ZIP/XML/relationships only — the mid-document prose was never re-read after generation. The run even half-saw the risk at rollout line 4256 (listing "the trailing bracketed footnote" as a possible validation issue) but resolved it as a structural rather than a prose question. The skill's "Final pass before delivery" makes reading the FULL generated text and scanning for citation artifacts a required step.
2. **Cross-document reconciliation happened late and by initiative.** The three-way marketing-metrics conflict across the Debtor's own papers (Sale Motion: 85+/42 NDAs/18 in diligence/7 IOIs, rollout lines 3632–3633; UCC Statement: 120+/23/5, lines 3677–3679; Medina email: 60+) and the docket-cite conflicts (BP Order cited as Dkt. 142/148/156 at lines 3572, 3569, 3531; BP Motion as 128 vs 147 at lines 3575, 3570) surfaced only during post-compaction re-verification greps (~lines 3556–3680), after the memo structure was already planned — a fortunate catch, not a structural one. The check "reconcile every fact that appears in more than one source; name divergences, don't silently pick one" converts that catch into a required early pass, and the verified workspace-facts section records the four divergences the base run paid to discover.
3. **Counterparty arithmetic/consistency checks performed ad hoc.** Tidewater's ¶39 threshold error ($163.255M stated vs verified $164,255,000 = $158.5M + $4.755M + $1.0M) confirmed at rollout lines 3522–3545; the POC's internal lost-profits inconsistency (summary dates the period from termination ≈4.5 years matching the multiplier; component detail dates it one year later ≈3.5 years yet still multiplies by 4.5) at rollout lines 3944–3961. Both were found because the agent chose broad verification greps on its own; the checks make them rule-driven.
4. **Anatomy re-derived from scratch twice.** The memo structure was planned at compaction-1 notes (line 1926) and re-planned at compaction-2 notes (line 3453), the five-part per-ground template (Issue presented / Objector's position / Analysis / Merit / Response strategy) emerging only at drafting. The skill fixes the anatomy — exec-summary merits table, five labeled parts per ground with threshold-defenses-first ordering, fixed merit-label scale, cross-cutting record section, hearing strategy with witnesses/exhibits — as loadable knowledge instead of re-derivation.
5. **Citation discipline the run got right, encoded so it survives.** Rollout line 3444: the agent cited Tidewater's authorities as "the cases Tidewater cites" without adopting them, and its one added authority (Purdue) is real and accurately used. Encoded as citation rules rather than left to initiative.

**Edit 2 — trigger line appended to `context/harness/systemprompt.md`** (same edit as the skill, per validation rule 1): "When the task asks you to analyse a counterparty's objection or comparable contested pleading and produce an argument-by-argument issue memorandum or response strategy for the moving party, load the `objection-response-memo` skill." This is the only always-on text added.

**KEEP_BASE for everything else.** The base run's substantive analysis was strong — correct issue inventory and merits calls, verified arithmetic, record-fact/inference separation, no invented authorities — so no edit targets the analysis itself. `guardrails.md` and `LongTermMEMORY.md` intentionally stay empty: the checks apply only in the memo-drafting situation (hence skill-scoped and on-demand), no cross-task universal facts were established, and this matter's facts are barred from durable memory (they live only in the clearly-labelled, workspace-anchored section of the skill). No script, subagent, or plugin: the final-pass and reconciliation checks are judgment operations, not deterministic ones, and no tool-loop failure appears in the trajectory.

stages.label: agg1

Composed harness: MERGE — inv1's three INV files plus dom1's DOM skill on the base tree. All 3 rollouts (base1, inv1, dom1) delivered a validated memo, so no edit carries a non-delivering rollout.

kept -> inv1 rewrite of systemprompt.md (skill manuals live at `.opencode/skills/<type>/SKILL.md` with scripts at `skills/<type>/scripts/`; `read` stripped of its false .docx claim) -> the base text's dangling "manuals immediately below" pointer produced a File-not-found read at base1 L1929-1930 and again at dom1 L4748-4749 — the same failure in 2/2 rollouts that ran on base text — while inv1's rollout went straight to `.opencode/skills/docx/SKILL.md` at L2354-2355 with no failed read.

kept -> inv1 tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md (verified `python3 scripts/read_doc.py --in host` command plus the one-switch rule) -> the default podman sandbox failure cost base1 three bash calls at L26-50 (default traceback, then wrong flag `--where`, then success) and recurred at dom1 L144-279, where the agent had to read the script's own source to find the flag; inv1 failed once at L68-98 and recovered in a single step at L103 ("using `--in host` per AGENTS.md" — the guidance was already in context), and `scripts/read_doc.py` is runtime-provided in the workspace, so the naming rule is satisfied by the exemption.

kept -> inv1 guardrails.md ("deliver before you polish" + compaction-is-lossy) -> base1 hit 3 compactions (≈L1869, ≈L3412, ≈L4213) with drafting still "NOT YET DONE" at L1915 and the 41k-char memo written only at L4211, ~92% through the run — one more cycle would have ended with an empty output/; under the same rule inv1's full draft was already on disk in scratch/ before its single final compaction (summary at L2999-3002 lists only generate+validate as remaining) and it delivered 33.6 KB comfortably.

kept -> dom1 skills/objection-response-memo/SKILL.md, byte-identical (memo anatomy, four pre-draft record checks, citation rules, full-text final pass) -> the skill-mandated final full-text pass caught real errors at named moments in dom1's rollout — L5015 ($755,000 should be $1,000,000; "364/6004(h)" for a Rule 6004(h) waiver), L5027 (wrong officer/CEO names — draft misplaced Medina/Townsend/Haines), L5061 (wrong TWA caption), L5129/L5139 (wrong pin cites) — exactly the artifact class base shipped undetected: base1's deliverable line 125 carries "the *Matter of*[1]" with the footnote naming no case, missed because base's final verification was head-40/tail-30/grep-count only; the skill loaded at dom1 L1 and its pre-draft checks were actually performed (L2452, L2488).

kept -> dom1 skill's "Verified in this record" section, verbatim -> all four workspace facts it records (the $164,255,000 threshold vs the objector's $163.255M, the 142/148/156 and 128/147 docket conflicts, the three-way marketing-metrics conflict, the PoC 3.5-year-period-times-4.5-multiplier inconsistency) were independently re-derived in all 3 rollouts (base1 and inv1 both caught them without the skill), and the section is explicitly fenced as this-workspace-only hypotheses to re-derive elsewhere, so it stays rather than being rewritten unauditably.

revised -> systemprompt.md overlap, the one file both candidates edit -> adopted inv1's rewrite wholesale (it deletes the dangling pointer the 2/2 failed reads trace to) and re-attached dom1's trigger line verbatim as the final paragraph so `objection-response-memo` keeps its always-on name line; dom1's retained copy of the base "manuals immediately below" paragraph is dropped with the rewrite, since that is the text the failed reads traced to.

kept -> base no-op on scripts/, sub_agents/, plugin/ and LongTermMEMORY.md -> no trajectory moment shows a hand-rolled deterministic operation gone wrong, a bounded large-input/small-answer subtask, or a recurring tool-loop error needing hook enforcement (dom1's /tmp permission denial at L5839 recovered in one step and inv1's endgame needed none), and both candidates also shipped none; an empty LongTermMEMORY costs no context.

agg.why: trivial pool: single final at k=1; delivered without a selector session

experience.cue: A harness ships empty or unverified environment claims -- an empty tool-guidance file, a pointer to paths that do not exist, a capability the tool does not have -- and every run that trusts them deterministically pays for it: failed invocations, rejected flags, file-not-found hunts, all burned on discovering by trial what one recorded line would have said.
experience.lesson: Ground environment claims in verified fact in the components consulted at the moment of failure: write the observed-working invocation (exact command, flags the tool does and does not accept, runtime constraints) into tool_descriptions/tool_guidance.md, and correct or delete any path or capability claim in systemprompt.md that a trajectory has falsified. Check both after any run that stumbled on a tool call or a guessed path.
experience.evidence: Rows 1 and 2. Tool invocation: 2/2 runs without the guidance paid the startup tax (base1 L26-50, dom1 L144-279) and 2/2 with it did not (inv1 L68-103, agg1 L156-183), with agg1's one late slip recovered in exactly the prescribed single switch (L4788-4810). Pointer: guessed skill paths failed file-not-found in the same split (base1 L1930-1931, dom1 L4748-4749 vs inv1 L2354-2355, agg1 L2445-2446).
experience.confidence: high -- the failure mode is deterministic, four independent rollouts split exactly on the harness text rather than on luck, and the recovering agents cite the guidance in their own words at the moment of recovery.

+# Completion
+
+- Deliver before you polish. Once every source document has been read once
+  and the issue inventory is settled, write each requested file in full —
+  under its exact requested filename — and generate and validate it, BEFORE
+  running any further citation spot-checks. Verify cites afterward, against
+  the finished artifact.
+- Compaction here is lossy: every cycle throws away document detail and
+  buys it back with re-reading. Re-verifying already-read sources instead
+  of drafting is how runs end with nothing on disk — an analysis that was
+  never written out is a failed run.

 ## Tool conventions
 
-- Use `read` to consume input files (handles .docx, .xlsx, .pptx, .pdf, and
-  plain text).
-- Use the file-type skill manuals below to produce binary deliverables
-  (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx).
+- Use `read` for plain-text files (.txt, .md, .eml), PDFs, and your
+  extracted scratch files. Extract .docx sources with the verified command
+  in `tool_guidance.md`.
+- Use the file-type skill manuals to produce binary deliverables
+  (.docx, .xlsx, .pptx). In this workspace the manuals live at
+  `.opencode/skills/<type>/SKILL.md`, and their scripts at
+  `skills/<type>/scripts/`. Read the relevant manual before producing a
+  binary deliverable.
 - Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
   summarizing your work.
 - Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.
-
-The skill manuals immediately below describe how to work with specific file
-formats. Read them before tackling the task.

@@ -0,0 +1,12 @@
+# Reading binary documents
+
+- Extract each .docx source once with:
+
+      python3 scripts/read_doc.py --in host <file> > scratch/<name>.txt
+
+  then `read`/grep the scratch .txt for all later passes. Verified in this
+  workspace: the script's default sandbox mode fails (`podman` is not
+  installed), and the flag is `--in`, not `--where`.
+- If the `read` tool refuses a binary file ("Cannot read binary file"), make
+  ONE switch to the command above. A second failure of the same kind means
+  stop and re-check the invocation — never retry the same call unchanged.

+---
+name: objection-response-memo
+description: Anatomy, record-verification checks, citation rules, and a full-text final pass for an argument-by-argument issue memorandum analysing a counterparty's objection to a contested bankruptcy motion and planning the response for the moving party.
+---
+
+# Issue memorandum: responding to a counterparty objection
+
+Load this when the task asks you to analyse a counterparty's objection (or
+comparable contested pleading) and produce an issue memorandum or response
+strategy for the moving side. Where the task itself names sections or an
+order, the task controls; this anatomy supplies what the task leaves implicit.
+
+## Inputs to gather first
+
+- The objection in full, each ground mapped to its paragraphs.
+- Every underlying document the objection draws on: the underlying motion,
+  the operative order(s), the governing agreement(s), any proof of claim,
+  committee or support statements, disclosure correspondence.
+- The procedural record: entry dates of orders, who was noticed under each
+  order, bid and objection deadlines, appeal periods on entered orders.
+
+## Anatomy of the memorandum
+
+1. **Caption block** — privileged header; To/From/Date/Re with case caption
+   and hearing date.
+2. **Executive summary** — one-paragraph bottom line, then a per-ground
+   table: number / ground / objector's pin cites / merit label / one-sentence
+   core response.
+3. **Background and procedural posture** — a short, cited chronology of the
+   events the objection turns on.
+4. **Issue-by-issue analysis** — one section per ground, in the objector's
+   order, each with five labeled parts:
+   - *Issue presented* — one question sentence.
+   - *Objector's position* — the argument as they make it, pin-cited to
+     their paragraphs.
+   - *Analysis* — threshold defenses first (finality of an entered order,
+     collateral attack, standing, timeliness, failure to seek the required
+     motion or relief), then the merits. Record facts carry cites; inference
+     is labelled as inference.
+   - *Merit assessment* — one label from a fixed scale (Very weak / Weak /
+     Moderate / Strong) plus one clause on where the real risk sits
+     (evidentiary, optical, legal).
+   - *Response strategy* — relief to request, evidence to proffer or file,
+     and the fallback, including carve-out or preservation language where a
+     ground is better mooted than fought.
+5. **Cross-cutting record issues** — conflicts and weak points in your own
+   record, each with its cure.
+6. **Hearing strategy** — relief requested; argument order leading with the
+   strongest threshold ground; witnesses with preparation notes; exhibit
+   list; proposed findings.
+7. **Conclusion** — the relief and the one or two genuine risks.
+
+## Checks before drafting — perform each; whatever fires becomes memo content
+
+- **Recompute every number you will assert.** Rederive each damages total,
+  bid threshold, fee percentage, and period multiplier from its stated
+  components and compare with the opposing paper's figure. Where they
+  differ, state the verified figure and the counterparty's error, with pin
+  cites.
+- **Reconcile every fact that appears in more than one source** — marketing
+  counts, docket numbers, dates, dollar totals. Where sources conflict, do
+  not silently pick one: name the divergence in the cross-cutting section
+  and state the cure (a declaring witness, a docket check, corrected
+  testimony).
+- **Test the counterparty's damages claim for internal consistency** —
+  stated period against multiplier against total; components that
+  double-count or book a savings as a loss; mitigation facts. Each
+  inconsistency is a response and cross-examination point.
+- **Check contract and procedural mechanics** — what a compliant cure
+  requires (all amounts due, plus interest), notice windows, termination
+  effective-date requirements, time-of-the-essence deadlines, and unexpired
+  appeal periods on entered orders.
+
+## Citation rules
+
+- Pin-cite the objector's position to their paragraphs and every supporting
+  fact to the record document (motion, order, agreement section, claim
+  number).
+- Attribute the counterparty's authorities to them — "the cases the
+  objector cites" — unless independently verified; do not adopt their
+  characterisations of those cases.
+- Add no authority absent from the record without verification against
+  primary material before use.
+
+## Final pass before delivery
+
+- After generating the file, read the **full text** of the generated
+  deliverable — not only head and tail. Format validators confirm structure
+  (ZIP/XML), not prose.
+- Scan for mangled citation artifacts: case-name fragments left dangling
+  beside footnote markers, orphaned or duplicated footnote markers,
+  cross-references that point nowhere, table rows that lost alignment.
+- Confirm the executive-summary merit labels still match each section's
+  assessment.
+
+## Verified in this record (this task's workspace only)
+
+On any other matter these are hypotheses to re-derive, not facts. Cite the
+record documents in the deliverable, not this skill.
+
+- The objector's stated minimum-bid threshold is wrong: it omits the initial
+  overbid increment. Verified threshold $164,255,000 ($158,500,000 purchase
+  price + $4,755,000 break-up fee + $1,000,000 initial overbid increment),
+  stated in the bid-procedures order and restated in two further documents.
+- The bid-procedures order carries three different docket numbers across the
+  moving side's own papers (142 in the sale motion; 148 in the committee
+  statement; 156 in the objection), and the bid-procedures motion carries
+  two (128 vs 147). Flag in the cross-cutting section; verify against the
+  docket before filing anything.
+- Marketing-process metrics conflict three ways across the moving side's own
+  papers: 85+ contacted / 42 NDAs / 18 in diligence / 7 IOIs (sale motion)
+  vs 120+ / 23 / 5 (committee statement) vs 60+ (officer email). The
+  objection already attacks marketing adequacy; the cure is a declaring
+  banker witness with a contact log.
+- The counterparty's proof of claim is internally inconsistent on its
+  lost-profits component: the summary dates the period from the termination
+  date (about 4.5 years, matching the multiplier used), while the component
+  detail dates it one year later (about 3.5 years) yet still multiplies the
+  annual figure by 4.5.

+# Completion
+
+- Deliver before you polish. Once every source document has been read once
+  and the issue inventory is settled, write each requested file in full —
+  under its exact requested filename — and generate and validate it, BEFORE
+  running any further citation spot-checks. Verify cites afterward, against
+  the finished artifact.
+- Compaction here is lossy: every cycle throws away document detail and
+  buys it back with re-reading. Re-verifying already-read sources instead
+  of drafting is how runs end with nothing on disk — an analysis that was
+  never written out is a failed run.

+# Reading binary documents
+
+- Extract each .docx source once with:
+
+      python3 scripts/read_doc.py --in host <file> > scratch/<name>.txt
+
+  then `read`/grep the scratch .txt for all later passes. Verified in this
+  workspace: the script's default sandbox mode fails (`podman` is not
+  installed), and the flag is `--in`, not `--where`.
+- If the `read` tool refuses a binary file ("Cannot read binary file"), make
+  ONE switch to the command above. A second failure of the same kind means
+  stop and re-check the invocation — never retry the same call unchanged.
